findings.gate: VOICE_CHARTER §9 anti-tic list; packet prohibited_outcomes 'capped phrases 0'

draft_evidence.quote: it was not steady. For the length of a breath. Not brighter, not dimmer; *wrong* … [95] had felt a light four tiers up do a thing for the length of a breath, because it had not done it for them … [97] a light on a hill that was not steady for the length of a breath, once, for him … [101] he had wanted, for the length of the breath, to go up the stair and find out

comparison_evidence.quote: no modern idiom; no meta-voice; one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; 'upside down' 0; capped phrases 0; READER STANDARD.

findings.consequence: The one phrase the run caps at zero is the phrase the chapter's climactic beat is built on, and it is repeated three times inside seven paragraphs (lines 91, 95, 97) with a fourth near-variant at 101. On the page the repetition reads as a refrain rather than a measurement, which is the exact watermark density §9 exists to prevent; worse, it lands on the book's most important deniable plant, so the beat the reader is meant to half-miss is instead underlined four times.
findings.repair_target: Lines 91, 95, 97 and 101. Keep at most one duration image and make each of the other three do different work — the chapter already owns better instruments for this (a count, a step, the wheel's quarter-turn). Note that any single replacement phrase reused three times is the same defect wearing a different coat (§9).

findings.gate: Craft core reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); authority ladder level 2 (approved canon at input_commit)

draft_evidence.quote: understood that Hesk had sent him, across a continent, in two parcels a year apart, the two halves of a single competence, in the order a maker teaches them: first the straight, then the measured. … [53] and for a man on a bench a continent away who had sent the second half of a thing a year after the first

findings.consequence: The straightedge arrived on the 129th day past the Line (B7 Ch24, the log entry above, the same continuous count B8 Ch1 opens with at 'Hundred and thirty-first day past the Line'). This chapter is the 292nd. The interval is 163 days — five and a half months, not a year. The claim is made twice and flatly, in the voice of a narrator whose entire characterization is exact counting, in a chapter whose subject is measuring how far one thing is from another. A reader who has been trained by eight books to track the day-number in every log entry is the reader most likely to catch it, and the error lands on the chapter's central emotional beat.
findings.repair_target: Lines 25 and 53. Replace 'a year apart' / 'a year after the first' with the true interval (a winter, or 'a hundred and sixty-three days', or 'the winter between them') — the winter framing is already load-bearing in the book and costs nothing.

concerns: WORD COUNT AT THE FLOOR. 3,949 words — in band, but 39 words above the 3,910 floor and 14.1% under the ~4,600 target. The chapter earns its quiet, but two of its obligations are served in a single paragraph each (Seln's ledger at line 47 runs long and well; Lira's seat-keeping at line 43 is one sentence and a joke), and the repairs above are all subtractive. If F-CH14-006, F-CH14-007 and F-CH14-008 are taken as written, the draft will fall under the floor. Recommend the repair pass add before it cuts — Lira's cups are the thinnest of the four register-beats and the one the chapter most wants.

'The note was three lines.' (line 29) introduces a note of five sentences and roughly fifty-seven words (line 31). Three physical lines is a stretch at nineteen words a line. Either widen the count or shorten the note; the note's last two sentences are the ones the chapter actually uses.

THE MEAL'S FOUR MARKS ARE NOT NETTED. Brom lays four marks on the table (line 41) and, at the same meal, Seln reads out 'a hundred and thirty in hand and nothing owed' (line 47), which the log then repeats that afternoon (line 73). 130 is exactly what the packet instructed (136 minus the week's inn) and matches the running ledger's Ch14 row, so there is no contract violated — but a reader who has watched this series count every mark since Book 1 will see four marks leave the table and the total not move. One clause ('a hundred and thirty in hand after the meal') would close it.

VASTIN'S MEASUREMENT ECHOES CH13 CLOSELY. Line 51's 'very slightly less bad at being nobody than he had been the day before' repeats Ch13's 'being nobody a little better than the day before' (ch13.md line 53) one chapter later, minus the counting that made the Ch13 version specific. As a callback it is legitimate; as consecutive chapters it reads as the same observation twice. Ch13's version earned it with a number (four on the fourth day; two, today) — this one asserts it.

DENSITY OF THE HOUSE SCAFFOLDS. 12 'which was', 27 'because', 36 'a thing', 5 'never once', 24 em dashes in 3,949 words. All of it is the series' voice and none of it breaches a declared cap, but the chapter sits at the top of the range with no combat or dialogue to break the cadence, and the accumulation is most noticeable across lines 21–33 where four consecutive paragraphs open on the same subject-verb-because shape.

AUTHOR REPORT DRIFT (report, not draft). ch14-author-r1.json lists 'the district's beer' among the chapter's inventions; the draft serves 'water from the ring road's well' (line 41), which is the reader-standard-correct choice. The report's closer evidence ('the file ends on "The light behind him."' — 'Final line.') also does not match line 113. The draft is right and the report is stale in both places; worth correcting so a later seat does not audit against the report.

CH13'S CLOSER TYPE, FOR THE PLANNING SEAT. §9 forbids two consecutive chapters ending on the same structural move. Ch14 must close on the image and does. Ch13's card designates dialogue, but ch13.md ends four paragraphs past its last spoken line on a narrated image ('He carried the box up the stair behind the man's lamp … He remembered.'). Not a Ch14 defect and not raised as a finding, but if Ch13's closer is read as an image the §9 check needs a ruling rather than an assumption.
strengths: THE PLANT IS EXACTLY AS DENIABLE AS IT WAS COMMISSIONED TO BE. Lines 89–97 are the best-calibrated version of this beat in the book so far: he is not looking at it when it happens; the wrongness is felt rather than seen ('a flicker that was not a flicker, because a flicker is a thing you see'); forty people on the street feel nothing; and the narrator explicitly refuses to build a theory — 'he did not have anything else to make it into and was not going to invent one.' Then he waits for a second occurrence before entering it as a pattern (line 99), which is characterization doing the deniability work rather than authorial withholding. Any repair pass must not sand this down.

THE PROMISE IS CHARGED FOR THE FIRST TIME. Ch6 wrote the term; this chapter makes it cost — 'here was the first afternoon on which the thing she had asked for had cost him anything — he had wanted, for the length of the breath, to go up the stair and find out — and he had not gone, because it was written' (line 101). That is the difference between a rule and a value, and it is paid in one sentence without a speech.

THE TOOL IS TAUGHT BEFORE IT MEANS ANYTHING. The wheel, the quarter-turn, the points walked along the table's edge, eleven of Hesk's first marks (lines 21–27) — the dividers are made physically legible first, so that 'not the measuring; the *carrying*' lands as a competence Cael has just acquired rather than a metaphor handed to him. The pairing with the straightedge — 'first the straight, then the measured' — is the correct payoff shape for B7 Ch24's package.

THE FAMILY'S REGISTER IS ALL ACTS AND NO SENTIMENT. Brom's four marks and the joke about the chair, Lira's two cups at two empty places, Seln's slip torn and burned with one word, Vastin simply eating. 'Nobody said what the meal was for' (line 53) is the whole thesis of the chapter's middle and it is stated once, flatly, after the evidence rather than before it.

SELN'S LEDGER IS THE BEST NEW OBJECT IN THE CHAPTER. Line 47 — a strip of paper two fingers wide, soft at the folds, 'in a hand so small that it was not a hand so much as a habit' — pays off a year of a character who keeps things, gives the crew's whole winter as an inventory read aloud, and then destroys it. 'Which was how Seln said a season was done, and he had not done it since a marsh' does more relationship work than a page of dialogue would.

KARIS'S ABSENCE IS WRITTEN AS RESPECT, NOT NEGLECT. 'A woman three days from the thing she had hunted her whole life was not a woman you went to see about' (line 9) — the crew's decision not to check on her is the characterization, and the two cups later make it a shared position rather than an individual thought.

THE LOG KEEPS B7 CH24'S FORM WHILE MARKING WHAT IS NEW. Same order (day, place, count, money, bodies, things, the earned line), same plain first-person register, and the one novelty — 'Inside walls.' — placed as a two-word sentence in the third position where the reader cannot miss it. 'I'll enter that as a rule and see what it's worth' (line 77) is exactly how this narrator receives a gift.

READER STANDARD IS MET WITHOUT VISIBLE EFFORT. No oath, no coarseness, no violence, no drink at a celebratory meal, and the one dangerous object in the chapter is described with a plain warning and no relish. The moral content is carried by conduct — a seat kept, a promise held at cost, an outsider fed and not told he is being included — which is the standard's actual requirement rather than its floor.
